generated_from.description: Started by todo_sync.py init; items added by todo_sync.py add from open GitHub issues.

ranking_method.score: value / sqrt(cost), multiplied by (1 + unblock_bonus) when the item unblocks at least one item
tie_breakers: primary source type, where the primary source is sources[0]: gh_issue, then impl_stub, then research_folder
primary source ref: issue number ascending for gh_issue, otherwise the ref path in code-point order
primary source item text in code-point order (absent item sorts first)

impact_definitions.silent_wrong_output: A shipped path completes without error or warning and publishes a value or feature that is wrong under an established rule.
impact_definitions.data_correctness: Output or reference data can be wrong or ungoverned, but the correct value still needs a rule or decision to define it, a guard is missing, or the wrong value already surfaces with a warning or error.
impact_definitions.runtime_failure: A path raises or aborts on an input it accepts.
impact_definitions.dev_velocity: Tests, CI or developer tooling are slower, noisier or less trustworthy than they need to be; no output changes.
impact_definitions.maintainability: Structure, duplication, dead code, missing tests or latent defects that no current production path reaches; no output changes.
impact_definitions.docs_tooling: Documentation, research records, configuration or agent tooling outside the shipped paths.

severity_scale.1: Cosmetic or hygiene: renames, dead code, stale docs, a test gap for working or accepted behavior.
severity_scale.2: Debt with a concrete cost, a latent defect that no current path reaches, a missing guard, or a defect that needs a rare or optional input.
severity_scale.3: A wrong or failing result on a supported but uncommon input, or a defect a warning already surfaces.
severity_scale.4: Wrong published output on a common input of a production path, or a failure that blocks a supported workflow.
severity_scale.5: Crashes or corrupts a production path on its normal inputs.

ranking_method.notes: Each item's severity, impact, LoE and blast radius come from its source's triage. Ranking compares scores rounded to 4 decimals; the tie breakers apply in order, so ids and ranks are reproducible from the item fields alone.

items.title: `amend-commit-msg` Suppress Output
items.decision_question: Run amend-commit-msg as a subagent (quiet, but it loses the conversation that is the reason it runs in the main session), or keep it in the main session and move the skeleton edits into a script call so no Update diff is printed?
items.summary: An amend-commit-msg run prints every Update of the skeleton JSON, with whole message strings, into the session; the issue wants it to run as a subagent or at least skip that output. Checked: plugins/harness/skills/amend-commit-msg/SKILL.md:9-10 runs the skill in the main session on purpose, because branch-commit-msg's fork has no view of the conversation; :98 tells it to edit the message strings of the skeleton JSON, which produces the Update output; its frontmatter (lines 2-4) has no context or agent key. The skill landed in PR #82 for #77.
items.proposed_change: After the decision: either add a script step (for example a branch_commit_msg.py subcommand that sets one block's message from a file or argument) so the skill writes messages with one Bash call instead of Edit, or split the run so a harness:messenger subagent gets the amendment request and the conversation facts it needs and returns only the saved path and commit list.

blast_radius.reasoning: One skill's execution path; the TXT it saves is unchanged.

loe.reasoning: A script subcommand or a frontmatter and dispatch change, plus a contract test.

items.why_ranked: Severity 2 dev_velocity: every amendment floods the main session with JSON diffs; size S.

items.title: Detached Worktree Skill (`d-w`) Needs a Complimentary Attach Worktree (`a-w`) Skill
items.summary: Moving changes back from a detached-HEAD worktree costs turns; the issue asks for an a-w skill that takes a target branch, either moves the worktree's commits (--committed) or stages the changes uncommitted on that branch, and removes the worktree afterwards without asking. Checked: plugins/harness/skills/d-w/SKILL.md:30-32 leaves the commits on a detached HEAD and cleanup to the developer, and plugins/harness/skills/d-w/commands/new_worktree.py is the only command; no a-w skill exists under plugins/harness/skills. plugins/harness/scripts/parallel2.py:383-399 already stages a worktree's committed diff onto a checkout by three-way apply, a candidate for the uncommitted mode.
items.proposed_change: Add plugins/harness/skills/a-w/SKILL.md and a command script taking --target_branch and --committed: verify the target branch is checked out in the main checkout and its tree is clean, then either cherry-pick the worktree's commits since its base sha onto the target (--committed) or three-way apply their combined diff into the index (reuse the parallel2 apply_lane approach), report conflicts and stop on them, and remove the worktree with git worktree remove once the move succeeds. Cross-reference it from d-w's Afterward section and add the README row and tests.

blast_radius.reasoning: A new skill with no existing consumers; d-w only gains a pointer.

loe.reasoning: A new skill and command with two move modes, conflict handling, worktree removal and git-backed tests.

items.why_ranked: Severity 2 dev_velocity: every d-w run ends in a manual, turn-costly re-attach; size M for a new skill and command.

items.title: pytest-scope: project-level enablement and a project-supplied hint in the broad-run deny message
items.summary: Gap 1: require_test_file and python are plugin options read from user settings only, so a project cannot commit the broad-run deny and a fresh machine gets no deny and no warning. Gap 2: the deny message cannot point at the project's own test lookup. Checked: plugins/pytest-scope/hooks/register.ts:12 reads options.require_test_file only; plugins/harness/hooks/_allow_settings.py:40-43 documents that pluginConfigs lives in user (or managed) settings only; plugins/pytest-scope/hooks/scope.ts:581-590 builds the deny text from the rule line, the git ls-files listing and the override line, with no project input; no pytest_scope or deny_hint key exists under plugins/.
items.proposed_change: Read a pytest_scope object from .claude/harness.json (require_test_file, optionally python and deny_hint), the project value winning over the plugin option and neither set meaning off. Append deny_hint as its own line to denyMessage after the file listing; without it the message stays byte-identical. Add the keys to defaults.json, harness.schema.json, the config dataclass and builder and the README key table, mirror the defaults in the mod with a mirror test, and cover both enablement paths and the hint in scope.test.ts. The optional file-list command in place of git ls-files is lower priority and can stay out of the first change.

blast_radius.reasoning: A new harness.json key touches the four config places and the pytest-scope mod; default behavior stays off.

loe.reasoning: Project-config reading in the TypeScript mod, a new config key in four places, a mirror test and deny-message tests.

items.why_ranked: Severity 2 dev_velocity: a guard a project cannot switch on goes missing silently on new machines; size M for a config key across the plugin and the mod.

items.title: Consolidate `merge-commit` SKILL --> `merge-commit-msg`
items.summary: merge-commit holds merge_body.py, but merge-commit-msg is the name that follows the commit-message skill convention; the issue asks to keep the best of both SKILL.md files in merge-commit-msg, move the scripts there and bring it in line with branch-commit-msg and c-msg and their scripts. Checked: plugins/harness/skills/merge-commit/commands/merge_body.py is the only script and merge-commit-msg holds only SKILL.md; plugins/harness/skills/merge-commit/SKILL.md:3 builds the merge body from the commit-message TXT files and points to merge-commit-msg for a PR-commit draft, while plugins/harness/skills/merge-commit-msg/SKILL.md:4-5 (model: haiku, effort: low) and :24-28 draft from three gh calls with no script. tests/skills/test_merge_body.py and tests/contract/test_root_separation.py name merge_body.
items.proposed_change: Merge the two SKILL.md files into plugins/harness/skills/merge-commit-msg/SKILL.md: keep the TXT-based merge_body.py path as the primary source and the gh-based draft as the fallback when no TXT exists; move commands/merge_body.py under merge-commit-msg, drive it the way branch-commit-msg and c-msg drive branch_commit_msg.py, delete the merge-commit skill folder, and update tests/skills/test_merge_body.py, tests/contract/test_root_separation.py, the README skill rows and docs/PROVENANCE.md if it maps merge_body.py.

blast_radius.reasoning: Removes a skill name developers invoke and moves a script that tests reference by path.

loe.reasoning: Two SKILL.md files to merge, a script move, test path updates and README rows.

items.why_ranked: Severity 2 maintainability: two overlapping skills route to each other and split one job; size M.

items.title: Add Flag option to `branch-commit-msg` to include a `merge-commit-msg`
items.summary: With a flag set, branch-commit-msg should kick off merge-commit-msg once its own run completes. Checked: plugins/harness/skills/branch-commit-msg/SKILL.md:4 argument-hint is [REF] [--base REF] [--fresh] [--no-fetch], with no merge flag, and the skill never names merge-commit or merge_body; it runs in a fork (plugins/harness/skills/branch-commit-msg/SKILL.md:6-7, context: fork, agent: harness:messenger). The TXT-based merge body builder is plugins/harness/skills/merge-commit/commands/merge_body.py, which #80 moves under merge-commit-msg. Unverified: whether a forked skill can invoke another skill; issue #9 records that a forked agent does not re-delegate.
items.proposed_change: Add a --merge flag to the branch-commit-msg argument-hint and SKILL.md: after build saves the TXT, the fork runs the merge body script (merge_body.py, at its merge-commit-msg path once #80 lands) and reports both paths. Land after #80 so the flag names the consolidated skill's script.

blast_radius.reasoning: An opt-in flag on one skill; the default run is unchanged.

loe.reasoning: A SKILL.md step and argument-hint change that calls an existing script.

items.why_ranked: Severity 1 dev_velocity: saves one skill invocation per branch; size S.

items.title: Add canned File-Message set (todo stuff)
items.summary: A change set made only of _IMPL_TODO.md, RepoToDo.json, ResearchImplementationCatalog.json and TODO_Snapshot_*.md files should get a predetermined commit message; this is the first preset for the #86 lookup. Checked: those names are configured, not fixed: this project's catalog is docs/TODO/RepoToDo.json (todo.catalog), and the stub name, research catalog and snapshot folder come from the todo.* keys that plugins/harness/lib/harness_lib/todo_sync/retire.py:219-245 reads (todo.research.catalog, todo.stub_name, todo.snapshots.dir). The TODO_Snapshot_*.md entry is a glob, so the #86 lookup needs pattern matching.
items.proposed_change: Once #86 lands, ship a default preset built from the configured todo.catalog, todo.research.catalog, todo.stub_name and todo.snapshots.dir paths rather than literal names (plugins stay generic), with one fixed message such as a chore(todo) subject, and test that a set holding any other file falls back to the drafter.

blast_radius.reasoning: One preset on top of the #86 lookup.

loe.reasoning: One preset derived from existing config keys and a test, after #86.

items.why_ranked: Severity 1 dev_velocity: saves drafting a routine catalog commit; size S, after #86.

items.title: pr-review: background execution via a saved workflow (Phases 1-3)
items.decision_question: Can a plugin ship a saved workflow, or must the pr-review skill write one under the consuming project's .claude/workflows/ (issue Q4)? The answer settles where the Phases 1-3 workflow lives before any of it is built.
items.summary: pr-review cannot fork like c-msg or pr-sum: Phase 2 fans out harness:pr-reviewer rows from the main session, a fork would break the per-row model floor, the Phase 5 sentinel binds to the session id, the bubble pause needs the developer and fixers write the shared tree. The issue proposes a saved workflow that runs capture, the reviewer fan-out and merge in the background and returns before amend; Phases 4-5 stay in the foreground. Checked: plugins/harness/skills/pr-review/SKILL.md has no context: key (frontmatter lines 2-5), unlike plugins/harness/skills/c-msg/SKILL.md:5-6 (context: fork, agent: harness:messenger); plugins/harness/hooks/check_phase5_sentinel.py:103 defines blocks_session(owner, session_id); plugins/harness/scripts/pr_review.py has no capture --json mode (its only --json is the gh pr view call at :333); dispatch_shape allows only parallel and inline in plugins/pr-review-watch/hooks/matrixRow.ts:15 and plugins/harness/schemas/pr_review_invocation_test_matrix.schema.json:57-61. Unverified: whether a workflow-launched agent inherits the parent's CLAUDE_CODE_SESSION_ID (Q2) and whether anything else parses capture's printed rows (Q1).
items.proposed_change: Settle Q4 first. Then add a capture --json mode to pr_review.py (or build the rows from the plan.json slots capture already writes), ship the Phases 1-3 workflow (capture, parallel harness:pr-reviewer agents with each row's model, merge) that stops after merge, add a Background mode section to the pr-review SKILL.md naming amend as the resume point and Phases 4-5 as foreground, and add dispatch_shape "workflow" to matrixRow.ts DISPATCH_SHAPES and the invocation matrix schema enum. Leave the Phase 5 workflow extension for later.

blast_radius.reasoning: Touches the pr-review skill, its capture driver and the reviewer-stats row shape shared with the pr-review-watch mod; the foreground path stays as it is.

loe.reasoning: A new workflow script, a structured capture output, a skill section, a schema enum and mod change, plus probes of the workflow runtime (Q2, Q4).

items.why_ranked: Severity 2 dev_velocity: a foreground pr-review blocks the session through the reviewer fan-out; size L for a new workflow, a capture mode and a schema change.

items.title: Add "auto-message" blocks for pre-determined change sets
items.decision_question: Does a change set qualify when every changed file matches some preset pattern (a subset), or only when it matches the preset exactly, and do the presets live in .claude/harness.json (a new config key in four places) or in plugin defaults?
items.summary: branch-commit-msg, c-msg and merge-commit-msg should use a preset commit message when the uncommitted changes, or one commit block, touch only files that match a preset file-name set. The issue sketches a Mapping[Set[str], str] lookup keyed by the set of normalized file names. Checked: c-msg and branch-commit-msg both drive plugins/harness/scripts/branch_commit_msg.py (plugins/harness/skills/c-msg/SKILL.md:11, :25), so one lookup there covers both; merge-commit-msg runs no script (plugins/harness/skills/merge-commit-msg/SKILL.md:24-28). No canned or auto-message code exists under plugins/harness/scripts or lib. As sketched, a set cannot be a dict key (a frozenset can), and exact-set lookup cannot serve a glob such as the TODO_Snapshot_*.md entry in #87.
items.proposed_change: After the decision, add a preset lookup (frozenset or pattern list mapped to a message) read from config, and have branch_commit_msg.py capture fill a block's message from the preset when the block's files all match one preset, leaving other blocks to the drafter; document the presets for c-msg, branch-commit-msg and, once #80 lands, merge-commit-msg.

blast_radius.reasoning: Changes the shared capture path of two commit-message skills and may add a config key.

loe.reasoning: Matching logic in the capture driver, a config surface and tests across two skills.

items.why_ranked: Severity 1 dev_velocity: a convenience for recurring change sets; size M for a shared capture change and config.

items.title: Add argument to `pr-sum` to include local changes
items.decision_question: pr_sum.py capture already includes staged, unstaged and untracked changes by default whenever the PR branch is checked out (commit 18f883f, PR #34), with --committed-only and --remote-head as opt-outs. Is an opt-in flag still wanted for a checkout that capture does not treat as the PR branch (a branch of another name, a worktree), or is the remaining work only the README, help and argument-hint updates?
items.summary: The issue asks for a pr-sum flag that diffs PR base..HEAD plus staged changes, with README, help and the hints block updated. Checked: plugins/harness/scripts/pr_sum.py:8-11 already runs the diff to the working tree (staged, unstaged and untracked) while a branch of the PR head's name whose HEAD contains that head is checked out, and :282-289 add --remote-head and --committed-only to turn it off; that landed in 18f883f ("PR Capture: defaults to include `--cached` (#34)", 2026-10-20), before the issue was opened on 2026-10-23. plugins/harness/skills/pr-sum/SKILL.md:60-64 documents it, but the argument-hint at plugins/harness/skills/pr-sum/SKILL.md:4 lists only PR, --level and --min-viz, and the pr-sum row at README.md:19 does not mention local changes.
items.proposed_change: After the decision: either add an explicit flag (for example --local) that forces the working-tree diff from the merge base when the checkout is not recognized as the PR branch, or keep the default and only document it. Either way add --committed-only and --remote-head (and any new flag) to the SKILL.md argument-hint, say in the README.md pr-sum row that a checked-out PR branch includes local changes, and keep the pr_sum.py --help text in step.

blast_radius.reasoning: The pr-sum capture options and its docs; existing default behavior is kept.

loe.reasoning: Documentation updates, plus at most one capture flag on an existing working-tree path.

items.why_ranked: Severity 1 docs_tooling: the behavior mostly exists and the gap is its documentation or an opt-in flag; size S.
